attrs.gap: Fable claimed assurance support and Embodiment support are one mathematical object. GPT-5.6 rejected that as stated and the rejection is correct: argument acceptability is NONMONOTONIC in the attack structure — adding an attack can remove acceptance and adding a defender can restore it — while Embodiment support is monotone only under EMB-MONOTONE-HYP. What survives is narrower and still real: after the attack semantics has fixed which support nodes are admissible, asking whether a sufficient positive support set remains IS a monotone question, and that second stage is the same computation Embodiment needs. R6 does not implement the sharing. The pipeline would be attack/defeat semantics, then admissible support nodes, then monotone sufficient-set evaluation, and only the third stage is common.
attrs.prior_art: Fable R5.2 F5 (ASR-SUPPORT-UNIFY) as rewritten by GPT-5.6 §4. Dung 1995 for the nonmonotonicity of acceptability under attack addition.
attrs.statement: Assurance and Embodiment can share one monotone sufficient-set engine, once domain-specific admissibility has been resolved.
